Definition: neuter of a presumed derivative of G4825; advisement; specially, a deliberative body, i.e. the provincial assessors or lay-court:--consultation, counsel, council.
BiblicalUsage: The Pharisees hold a council against Jesus to destroy Him, and at dawn all the chief priests and elders take counsel against Him to put Him to death. The word is not a fair court but a plot dressed as deliberation, and it shows how religion can organise itself against its own Lord.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that a council that plots against Christ is no council at all, and I believe I must watch my own heart for the same habit of deciding against Him in advance.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
